text.p: Turkish central bank funded banks a total of 33.39 trillion lira via money market operations on Monday as banks were squeezed for cash due to an extended five-day New Year holiday in the public sector, bankers said.
It lent banks 8.4 trillion lira overnight at 78 percent, 24.2 trillion lira via tomorrow/next value at 74 percent and 790 billion lira via tomorrow/week deals at 75 percent.
The central bank's total funding on Friday was slightly lower at 31 trillion lira. The average overnight money rate edged higher to 77.63 percent today from Friday's 77.45.
Despite cash shortage, the lira ended weaker at 108,020 to the dollar after Friday's 107,450 close, on a firmer dollar/mark pairty and continuing currency demand ahead of the New Year.

The central bank's move to raise its dollar rate for banks' compulsory currency transfers to 107,450 from 107,300 at opening in line with the parity also fuelled the dollar's gains in the afternoon, bankers said.

Turkish lira depreciated by 44.65 percent against the U.S. dollar in 1996, after a 35 percent loss in 1995. The central bank set its end-1996 official dollar bid rate at 107,505 lira, compared to 59,501 lira at the end of last year.

T-bill and bond yields dived by some six points as demand for outstanding papers surged on news that witholding tax will be raised to 12 pct from current 10 on interest income from government papers to be issued in 1997.

Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said on Friday the witholding tax would be raised and a plan to introduce income tax in 1998 on the previous year's interest earnings from government securities would be postponed.
He said investors were willing to pay higher witholding tax in 1997 instead of the "tedious task of filling tax forms" to declare and pay income tax in 1998 on interest income recorded in 1997.
Turkey had imposed the 10-percent witholding tax on interest income from t-bills and bonds to be issued from November 1 with 1997 maturity as part of the government's revenue raising packages.
The new 12 percent tax will be effective from January 2.

The average yield on the most active October 30,1997 paper dived to 105.98 percent, down 6.5 points from Friday. The second most active September 3, 1997 paper yielded 106.16 percent, down sharply from Friday's 112.35 average.
